sources.title: Status Assessment of Clarias Species in the Philippines: Insights from DNA Barcodes
sources.citation: Santos, B. S., Vesagas, F. P. C., Tan, M. T. C., Jumawan, J. C., & Quilang, J. P. (2015). Science Diliman, 27(2), 21-40.
sources.pantabanganEvidence: Table 1, printed p. 25, lists Philippines accessions KC789523-27 as Yambot et al. (unpublished). The article section “Additional Philippine sequences of C. batrachus,” printed p. 30, states five Pantabangan Dam Clarias batrachus COI sequences were included. NCBI GenBank records KC789523.1-KC789527.1 match those five names, PNT voucher codes, and explicit Pantabangan Dam locality qualifiers. This verifies the historical five-accession paper crosswalk; voucher custody and present-day occurrence are not independently verified.
sources.disposition: Historical published-analysis crosswalk for five Pantabangan Clarias batrachus sequences, not five independent confirmations or a current occurrence checklist. Keep app assertions at zero.

crossSourceFindings: The 2006 NAST abstract reports 12 endemic/indigenous taxa in Nueva Ecija, including four freshwater fish; the 2009 Silliman abstract reports ten indigenous plus one endemic taxon in Nueva Ecija. The three author overlap and five named Nueva Ecija waters overlap, so the values are related historical study outputs, not independent richness estimates; methods, taxonomy and survey periods need reconciliation.

The 2026 DNA article abstract exposes only five of its nine claimed species and still lacks an article-specific accession/voucher crosswalk. A separate 2013 GenBank submission resolves 40 fish accessions across nine submitted names; the 2015 Clarias paper independently crosswalks KC789523-27 to five Pantabangan Clarias batrachus sequences. The 2015 crosswalk verifies only that historical subset and does not establish that all 40 records are the 2026 article dataset. A third-party-indexed earlier thesis draft reports a different 12-species count and 43 samples, but its status, relationship to the paper and reuse basis are not verified; it is excluded from evidence extraction.
The 2024 largemouth-bass community paper's table and abstract agree on blackchin tilapia being counted in four boats, while its results prose says three. This is a source-internal count conflict.
A separate 2024 largemouth-bass diet paper reports only aggregate prey classes in its accessible abstract; it does not substantiate named prey taxa.

The 2026 DNA paper and 2015 Clarias barcode review both name Apolinario Yambot in connection with Pantabangan barcodes, but shared-project/specimen lineage has not been established; they cannot be treated as independent confirmations.

A bounded NCBI Nucleotide search found 40 fish COI accessions under a 2013 unpublished Pantabangan fish-barcode submission: 39 source qualifiers explicitly say Pantabangan Dam and one says only Nueva Ecija. Their nine submitted names and 40-record total match the 2026 article abstract aggregate, and the submissions share authors/project context; however, the 2026 article abstract gives no accessions, so identity of the sequence sets is unverified. The NCBI organism annotation for Micropterus is Micropterus salmoides floridanus while the abstract reports Micropterus floridanus. Keep the records as a separate historical accession dataset pending the full article/supplement crosswalk.

The 2015 Clarias paper supplies a specific published subset crosswalk: Table 1 lists accessions KC789523-27 under Yambot et al. (unpublished), and its discussion says those five Pantabangan Clarias batrachus sequences were analyzed. All five corresponding GenBank records have PNT vouchers and an explicit Pantabangan Dam locality. This is historical sequence evidence, not five independent confirmations of current occurrence.
scopeAndAccuracyLimits: No single reviewed source provides a current, complete Pantabangan fish checklist.
Survey periods, row-level capture locations, catchment/reach geometry and environmental class were not established for all candidate records.
Automated or source-reported names remain unreviewed against current taxonomy and individual specimen evidence.
Historical sampling, stocking, fishery catches, community perceptions and DNA sequences are different evidence types and must remain separate.
No source in this review supports current abundance, catchability, legal status or safety advice.
nextStep: Locate the full 2026 article or supplement and compare its accession table with the separate 2013 NCBI submission; keep the datasets distinct until an exact crosswalk is documented, then review current taxonomy and reuse terms.
